mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of sustained unemployment above 5.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, reducing corporate earnings expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in payroll employment above 200,000 persons per month signals strengthening labor market conditions, increasing corporate earnings expectations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of sustained increase in payroll employment above 200,000 persons per month (t-test p > 0.05).
